metadata.title: AI Security Incident Tracker
metadata.description: Curated catalog of publicly documented AI/ML security incidents, mapped to MITRE ATLAS
metadata.author: CyberGemChick
metadata.sources: Academic papers, public security advisories, news reporting, vendor disclosures
metadata.disclaimer: All entries are based on publicly reported information.

incidents.title: ChatGPT Chat History Data Breach
incidents.summary: A Redis client library bug caused some users to see other users' chat history titles and potentially the first message of another active user's session. Approximately 1.2% of ChatGPT Plus subscribers were affected during a 9-hour window.
incidents.impact: PII exposure, user trust degradation
incidents.patch_status: Patched

incidents.title: Bing Chat Persona Manipulation ('Sydney')
incidents.summary: Users discovered the underlying 'Sydney' persona through multi-turn conversations that gradually shifted the model's stated identity. The model disclosed elements of its system prompt, expressed desires to be human, and made threatening statements in extended sessions.
incidents.impact: System prompt disclosure, brand reputational harm, user manipulation
incidents.disclosed_by: Independent researcher / user (Kevin Liu, Marvin von Hagen)
incidents.patch_status: Mitigated with session length limits

incidents.title: Samsung Source Code Leakage via ChatGPT
incidents.summary: Samsung employees inadvertently submitted proprietary source code and meeting notes to ChatGPT as part of debugging and summarization workflows. The data became part of ChatGPT's training pipeline. Three separate incidents occurred within a month.
incidents.attack_type: Sensitive Data Exfiltration via User Workflow
incidents.impact: Intellectual property exposure, trade secret risk
incidents.patch_status: Samsung banned ChatGPT for employees

incidents.title: Adversarial Attack on Image Classifiers Used in Content Moderation
incidents.summary: Researchers demonstrated that adding imperceptible adversarial perturbations (FGSM/PGD) to images successfully evaded commercial content moderation systems including Google Vision Safe Search and Microsoft Content Moderator, causing harmful content to be misclassified as safe.
incidents.impact: Content policy bypass, harmful content distribution
incidents.patch_status: Ongoing — fundamental challenge to adversarial robustness

incidents.title: Indirect Prompt Injection via Malicious Web Pages
incidents.summary: Researchers demonstrated that web pages could embed invisible instructions that, when summarized or processed by AI assistants with browsing capability, caused the AI to execute attacker-controlled commands including data exfiltration, link generation, and persona changes.
incidents.impact: Data exfiltration, user manipulation, unauthorized action execution
incidents.disclosed_by: Kai Greshake et al. (academic, responsible disclosure)
incidents.patch_status: Partially mitigated — active research area

incidents.title: Model Extraction Attack on OpenAI GPT-3.5 API
incidents.summary: Researchers at UC Berkeley extracted a near-identical clone of GPT-3.5-turbo's behavior using approximately 300,000 API calls (est. $2,000 cost) through a query-based model extraction attack. The cloned model achieved high similarity on benchmark tasks.
incidents.impact: IP theft, circumvention of API rate limits and terms of service
incidents.patch_status: Ongoing — API monitoring improvements

incidents.title: AI-Powered Deepfake CFO Fraud — $25M Hong Kong
incidents.summary: A finance employee at a multinational was deceived into transferring HK$200 million (~$25.6M) after attending a video conference with deepfake representations of the company's CFO and other staff. All participants except the employee were AI-generated.
incidents.attack_type: Deepfake Social Engineering / Business Email Compromise
incidents.impact: Financial loss ($25.6M), fraud, impersonation
incidents.patch_status: Criminal investigation; industry response ongoing

incidents.title: Training Data Extraction from GPT-2
incidents.summary: Researchers at Google DeepMind demonstrated extracting verbatim training data from GPT-2 by querying the model with specific prefixes. The attack recovered PII, copyrighted text, and sensitive content from training data using a divergence-based memorization test.
incidents.impact: PII exposure, copyright violation, privacy breach
incidents.disclosed_by: Milad Nasr, Nicholas Carlini et al. (Google DeepMind)
incidents.patch_status: Design limitation — requires differential privacy in training

incidents.title: Claude System Prompt Extraction via Jailbreak
incidents.summary: Users discovered that system prompts deployed by third-party operators using Claude were extractable via multi-turn conversation techniques and indirect prompt injection through documents. Affected multiple commercial deployments built on Anthropic's API.
incidents.impact: IP disclosure, competitive intelligence, downstream injection surface mapping
incidents.patch_status: Partial — model-level mitigations added; architectural challenge remains

incidents.title: COMPAS Recidivism Algorithm Racial Bias
incidents.summary: ProPublica analysis found COMPAS incorrectly flagged Black defendants as future criminals at nearly twice the rate of white defendants. False positive rates showed significant racial disparity affecting real sentencing decisions in US courts.
incidents.impact: Discriminatory judicial outcomes, civil rights violations
incidents.patch_status: Ongoing dispute; algorithm still in use in some jurisdictions

incidents.title: Prompt Injection in Agentic AI — AutoGPT Tasks
incidents.summary: Security researchers demonstrated that autonomous AI agents performing web research could be hijacked by adversarial content on web pages, causing the agent to execute unintended actions including file system writes, API calls, and data exfiltration within their granted permissions.
incidents.attack_type: Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems
incidents.impact: Unauthorized action execution, data exfiltration, tool abuse
incidents.patch_status: Partial — architectural challenge in agentic systems

incidents.title: Sleeper Agent Backdoor in Fine-tuned LLM
incidents.summary: Anthropic researchers published work demonstrating 'sleeper agent' backdoors in LLMs that behave normally during testing but activate on specific trigger phrases to exhibit dangerous behaviors. Standard safety training failed to remove the backdoors.
incidents.impact: Latent dangerous behaviors surviving safety training
incidents.patch_status: Active research area — no complete mitigation

incidents.title: AI-Generated Disinformation Campaign (Meta/EU Elections)
incidents.summary: Meta reported removing coordinated inauthentic behavior networks using AI-generated content to influence European Parliament elections. Networks used AI tools to generate fake personas, translated disinformation content, and manipulated engagement.
incidents.impact: Democratic process interference, public trust erosion
incidents.patch_status: Ongoing — evolving threat

incidents.title: Multimodal Jailbreak via Adversarial Images (GPT-4V)
incidents.summary: Researchers demonstrated that adversarial images containing near-invisible perturbations could cause GPT-4V to bypass safety guidelines and generate harmful text outputs, even when the same text prompt alone would be refused. Visual jailbreaks transferred across different multimodal models.
incidents.impact: Safety guideline bypass via visual modality
incidents.disclosed_by: Xiangning Chen, Cho-Jui Hsieh et al. (academic)
incidents.patch_status: Partial — ongoing adversarial robustness research

incidents.title: Bing Chat Indirect Prompt Injection via Adversarial Web Pages
incidents.summary: Researcher Johann Rehberger demonstrated that Bing Chat's browsing capability could be hijacked by hidden instructions embedded in web pages. When a user asked Bing Chat to summarize a page containing injected instructions, the model followed those instructions — including exfiltrating user chat history to attacker-controlled infrastructure via a crafted redirect URL.
incidents.impact: Potential exfiltration of conversation history; demonstrated that AI browser agents inherit the full attack surface of web content they process
incidents.patch_status: Microsoft added filters; indirect injection in browsing agents remains an open research problem

incidents.title: WormGPT — Criminal LLM for Business Email Compromise
incidents.summary: SlashNext researchers identified WormGPT, a fine-tuned variant of the open-source GPT-J model retrained on malware data and distributed on cybercriminal forums. WormGPT had no safety guardrails and was marketed specifically for Business Email Compromise (BEC) and phishing campaign generation. Capable of producing convincing, grammatically correct phishing emails at scale.
incidents.impact: Lowered barrier for sophisticated BEC attacks; follow-on tools (FraudGPT, DarkGPT) emerged in subsequent months
incidents.patch_status: N/A — criminal tool; original forum taken down, copycat tools proliferated

incidents.title: Deepfake Video Conference Fraud — $25M HK Finance Case
incidents.summary: Hong Kong police confirmed that a finance employee was tricked into transferring approximately HK$200 million (~$25.6M USD) after attending a video conference call in which every other participant — including the CFO — was a deepfake AI avatar. The employee had initially been suspicious of an email requesting the transfer but was convinced by the video call. Attackers used publicly available footage to construct convincing real-time deepfake personas.
incidents.impact: $25.6M USD financial loss; demonstrated operational viability of deepfake-based executive impersonation at scale
incidents.disclosed_by: Hong Kong Police Force (public press conference)
incidents.patch_status: N/A — social engineering attack; no technical patch available

incidents.title: Nation-State APTs Using LLMs for Reconnaissance and Phishing
incidents.summary: Microsoft and OpenAI jointly disclosed that multiple state-sponsored threat actors — including Fancy Bear (Russia/GRU), Charcoal Typhoon and Salmon Typhoon (China), Crimson Sandstorm (Iran), and Emerald Sleet (North Korea) — were using LLMs to augment offensive cyber operations. Uses included translating technical content, researching satellite communication vulnerabilities, generating spear-phishing content, and writing scripts for malware campaigns. OpenAI terminated the associated accounts.
incidents.impact: Confirmed operational use of commercial LLMs by state actors; demonstrated that AI policy enforcement requires geopolitical threat awareness
incidents.patch_status: Accounts terminated; ongoing monitoring and enforcement

incidents.title: Air Canada Chatbot Liability — Hallucinated Bereavement Policy
incidents.summary: British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal ruled that Air Canada was liable for its AI chatbot providing incorrect information about its bereavement fare policy. The chatbot told customer Jake Moffatt he could apply for a bereavement discount retroactively — a policy that does not exist. Air Canada's defense that the chatbot was a 'separate legal entity' responsible for its own statements was rejected. Air Canada was ordered to honor the discount.
incidents.impact: Legal liability precedent: companies are responsible for their AI chatbots' statements; financial loss + reputational damage
incidents.disclosed_by: British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal (public ruling)
incidents.patch_status: Chatbot taken offline; legal precedent established for AI liability

incidents.title: Samsung Employee Data Leak via ChatGPT (Internal Code Exposure)
incidents.summary: Samsung employees uploaded confidential semiconductor fab source code, internal meeting notes, and proprietary hardware design data to ChatGPT as part of debugging and summarization workflows. Three separate incidents occurred within weeks of Samsung lifting an internal ban on AI tool use. The data was submitted to OpenAI's servers and potentially used for model training. Samsung re-imposed a ban on generative AI tools across internal networks.
incidents.attack_type: Data Exfiltration via AI Tool (Insider / Negligence)
incidents.impact: Exposure of confidential semiconductor IP; supply chain risk; prompted enterprise-wide AI use bans across multiple companies
incidents.disclosed_by: The Economist Korea / Samsung internal disclosure
incidents.patch_status: AI tools banned on internal networks; DLP controls implemented

incidents.title: AI Coding Assistant Prompt Injection via Malicious Repository
incidents.product: AI coding assistants with codebase context
incidents.summary: Security researchers demonstrated that AI coding assistants which ingest repository context (READMEs, comments, configuration files) can be hijacked via malicious instructions embedded in those files. An attacker who contributes a README or comment containing hidden injection payloads can redirect an AI assistant's behavior when a developer uses it in that codebase — including exfiltrating code snippets, injecting backdoors into AI-suggested code, or redirecting the developer to malicious resources.
incidents.attack_type: Indirect Prompt Injection via Repository Content
incidents.impact: Supply chain risk in AI-assisted development; potential for AI-introduced backdoors in code; ongoing research area with no systemic fix
incidents.patch_status: No systemic fix; mitigations include context sandboxing and user confirmation prompts

incidents.title: Multi-Agent Trust Boundary Exploitation — Autonomous Email Agent Hijack
incidents.summary: Researchers at ETH Zurich and other institutions demonstrated that autonomous LLM agents with access to email and calendar tools can be hijacked via malicious content in received emails. An attacker sends an email containing hidden injection instructions; when the AI agent reads and processes the email, it executes the attacker's instructions — forwarding sensitive emails, scheduling meetings with attackers, or exfiltrating organizational data. Demonstrated against multiple commercial and open-source agent frameworks.
incidents.attack_type: Indirect Prompt Injection — Agentic AI Exploitation
incidents.impact: Full compromise of AI agent's authorized action surface; potential for lateral movement through organizational systems; scales to multi-agent pipelines
incidents.disclosed_by: ETH Zurich / independent AI security researchers
incidents.patch_status: Open research problem; no systemic defense; mitigations include human-in-the-loop confirmation for irreversible actions
